compiled_state.description:
Scope: root-level `src/rebar/*.py` plus `attest/`, `metrics/`, `review_bot/`, `opcert_service/`, `audit/`, `grounding/`, `_guides/`. ~180 lines leave of 7,248 comment lines (2.5%) — this scope is in good health and the yield is concentrated, not diffuse.

SURFACED A LIVE DEFECT, filed separately: `_mcp_models.BridgeFsckOut` omits `binding_drift`, so the MCP outputSchema under-declares a field `bridge_fsck.py:217` always returns. The comment at `_mcp_models.py:31-34` claiming 'the cross-interface schema tests pin both to the canonical schema' is FALSE — those model names appear zero times in tests/. That false assurance is why the drift went unnoticed.

Two prior leads resolved AGAINST the hypothesis and belong in do_not_move: `_mcp_llm.py`'s 121 docstring lines are the literal wire-visible MCP tool descriptions FastMCP publishes to clients — API surface, not narration, zero recoverable. And `_config_schema.py`'s `# read-via:` markers are machine-consumed by `scripts/check_config_reads.py`, a CI gate — deleting one breaks CI.

Caveat that bounds this shard: 280 of `_config_schema.py`'s 792 lines are comments, and for many keys they are the ONLY documentation — `docs/config.md` has zero coverage for `completion_floor_active`, `comment_max_chars`, `auth_proxy_secret_env`. Recovering more than ~34 lines there requires writing those doc rows FIRST, or the trim destroys documentation rather than relocating it.

Three new ADRs proposed from `review_bot/`: bounded shutdown (drain/cancel/grace-period chain, test-pinned against docker-compose `stop_grace_period`); the deploy-safe in-flight counter and its deliberate over-count; retryable coverage gaps deferring vote-less under a bounded budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination [operator-attested]
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [x] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [x] No load-bearing invariant is lost
## CORRECTION (plan-review preempt, parent 373f disposition vocabulary)

Superseding ACs encode the 373f disposition rules and the verified state of this shard's claims.
KEY UPDATE: the shard's headline "SURFACED A LIVE DEFECT" is now STALE — that defect has already
been fixed on main (BridgeFsckOut now declares `binding_drift`, `_mcp_models.py` now correctly
cites the CI-enforced drift gate `python -m rebar.schemas.check_mcp_models --check`, and the
`test_mcp_model_schema_drift_*` tests now exist). So that comment is CORRECT-AS-IS → DO_NOT_MOVE,
NOT a correction target. The two documentation-load-bearing do_not_move findings are confirmed.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [x] Every substantial in-scope comment unit is dispositioned into exactly one parent-373f
      label: RELOCATE (to docs, reduced to a one-line citation), DELETE, KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE, or
      CORRECT-IN-PLACE. CORRECT if it documents current behavior/a live invariant; DELETE only
      when the referent is gone (record the reason in the commit body).
- [x] MOOT ITEM (do not re-correct): the `_mcp_models.py` schema-assurance comment is already
      accurate on current main — it cites the real CI drift gate and `BridgeFsckOut.binding_drift`
      already exists. Treat it as DO_NOT_MOVE (accurate). Do NOT delete or rewrite it, and do NOT
      re-file the already-fixed drift defect.
- [x] DO_NOT_MOVE (verified): `_mcp_llm.py`'s tool docstrings (~121 lines) are the wire-visible
      MCP tool descriptions FastMCP publishes to clients (API surface, zero recoverable);
      `_config_schema.py`'s `# read-via:` markers (12 of them) are machine-consumed by the CI gate
      `scripts/check_config_reads.py` (deleting one breaks CI). Both stay verbatim.
- [x] `_config_schema.py` documentation caveat (NO doc loss): ~280 of its lines are comments and
      for many keys they are the ONLY documentation (`docs/config.md` has no rows for
      `completion_floor_active`, `comment_max_chars`, `auth_proxy_secret_env`, etc). Recover more
      than the ~34 trivially-recoverable lines ONLY by writing the `docs/config.md` rows FIRST,
      then relocating; never trim a key's sole documentation.
- [x] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands.
- [x] Any ADRs proposed from `review_bot/` (bounded shutdown; deploy-safe in-flight counter;
      retryable coverage-gap deferral) are created only if they document a real current invariant,
      numbered from the next free ADR id, and cited from the code they explain rather than
      inlined.
- [x] The actual recovered comment-line count is measured by diff and recorded on this ticket as
      an OUTPUT, not a target. No load-bearing invariant is lost.
- [x] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass unchanged.
